Immortal Blaze is a Companion Story of Changli that takes place in Mt. Firmament, Huanglong.

Steps[]

  1. Roam in Hongzhen
  2. Ask around about Hongzhen (0/3)
  3. Find the Place "Next to a Ring and Hanging Eaves"
  4. Head to the Pavillion at 13:00-15:00
  5. Head to the Designated Location to See Changli
  6. Head into Mt. Firmament with Changli
  7. Find the Source of the Smell Abby Mentioned
  8. Enter the Cave
  9. Defeat the TDs and Rescue the Explorer
  10. Return to Hongzhen
  11. Ask around about the Explorer
  12. Go to the Hotel Where Fuling Stays
  13. Tell Xinyi what You Know
  14. Return to the Cave where You Met Wuli
  15. Investigate the Surroundings
  16. Keep Going Forward
  17. Go to the Area where Time Flows in Disorder
  18. Rewind the Weiqi Board's Time
  19. Learn about the Weiqi Board's Past
  20. Defeat the Fractsidus Artificers
  21. Enter the Sonoro Sphere and Reveal the Weiqi Board's Secrets
    1. Find Changli
    2. Follow the Voice Calling for Help
    3. Go to a Safer Location with the Little Girl
    4. Solve the Puzzle With the Little Girl
    5. Continue Forward
    6. Clear the Roadblock and Continue Forward
    7. Defeat the TDs in Your Way
    8. Continue Forward
    9. Find a Way to Get Inside Together
    10. Defeat the TDs Guarding the Ruins
    11. Go Deeper into the Ruins
    12. Investigate the Mechanisms inside the Ruins
    13. Connect the Light Beams inside the Mechanism
    14. Investigate the Familiar Mirage
    15. Find Rover
    16. Defeat the TDs in Your Way
    17. Clear the Roadbloack
    18. Continue Forward
    19. Investigate the Familiar Mirage
    20. Walk Through the Gate
    21. Solve Master Xuanmiao's Puzzles
    22. Connect the Light Beams inside the Mechanism
    23. Proceed to End the Sonoro Sphere
    24. Defeat the Chrono Shadow
  22. Rest for a While (Two Days)
  23. Learn about Changli's whereabouts with Xinyi
  24. Meet with Changli at the agreed location

Gameplay Notes[]

  • Completing the "Roam in Hongzhen" step awards the player Feather Pendant and Changli's Letter..
  • Completing the "Defeat the Chrono Shadow" will replace Feather Pendant with Flame Feather Pendant.
  • The location from the step (Find the Place "Next to a Ring and Hanging Eaves[1]"), is located at the very top of the building, next to the NPC Tanchuan.

Dialogue[]

Quest Description
You meet an old storyteller when you roam about in Hongzhen. While you listen to the the immortality tales about Mt. Firmament, you notice another interested listener...
(Head to the designated location)
Elder: ...The Weiqi pieces were scattered, but the guru remained calm. "It's getting late," he said gently to the woodcutter. "Shouldn't you be heading down the mountain?"
Elder: As he glanced at the sky, the woodcutter was shocked to see how much time had passed. "It couldn't have been more than two hours," he thought in disbelief. Feeling apologetic, he prepared to leave, worried that the guru would be annoyed with him.
Elder: But when the woodcutter turned around, he nearly jumped out of his skin. The hermit guru, who had been playing Weiqi and drinking wine, was now gone. In his place lay a shattered Weiqi board and a heap of decaying bones.
Elder: The woodcutter was so scared that he dropped his bamboo basket and ran down the mountain without even looking back.
Elder: As he reached the mountain's base, he was hit with a stark realization. The quaint village he remembered had bloomed into a bustling town, with sturdy brick houses replacing the humble thatched cottages. And where his home once stood, only an empty wasteland remained.
Elder: He noticed a date on the calendar that he had never seen before. In shock, he grabbed a passerby and urgently asked, "Excuse me, can you tell me the current date and time?"
Elder: As he heard the answer, his legs went weak. Everything had changed—time had passed and his loved ones were gone. No one remembered him anymore.
Perplexed Audience: So the woodcutter left Mt. Firmament, but how was he still alive and kicking? With a hundred year's worth of time inside him, shouldn't he...
Onlookers: Your story... It's a bit far-fetched, don't you think? I mean, if I wasn't from Hongzhen, I might have fallen for it.
Elder: ...Well! That's the whole point. The truth is stranger than fiction, my friend. Every detail in that story is based on real events.
Elder: Let me share with you the other legend of Mt. Firmament, for deep within its sacred peaks lies a powerful secret... the "Secret of Immortality"!
Elder: We all know that Mt. Firmament is the abode of the Sentinel, gathering spiritual energies from both heaven and earth for countless eons. Over time, even the mountain itself has taken on the form of our majestic Sentinel!
Elder: Living in the mountains for long stretches of time, surrounded by fresh air and drinking from nature's own bounty, can add years to one's life span!
Elder: It all starts with that game of Weiqi, one that the woodcutter stumbled upon. Too bad those secrets have been long forgotten ...
Elder: Gather around now, people. You're in for the story of a lifetime...
...Changli?
Changli: Shh...
Changli: ...I'll see you there.
Abby: *yawn* What's with the ruckus... Huh, whatʼs that in your hands?
Changli gave it to me a moment ago.
Abby: Hmm... "Behold Hongzhen in its entirety, next to a ring and hanging eaves. When eternal snow thaw into flowing streams, let us reconvene."
Abby: Ooh... I see, I see...
Do you know what it means?
Ooh... So that's how it is...
Abby: I see I've got no clue at all!
So much for the anticipation!
Wow, I'm so shocked to hear that.
Abby: I get the very last part, at least! She's asking you out! Well that's a fancy way to write stuff...
...The first part reads like it's about the meeting spot.
According to the description, it's somewhere in Hongzhen.
Abby: And now... this next sentence, "eternal snow thaw into streams"... What is that supposed to mean?
Maybe it has something to do with local folklore.
Abby: How did you manage to get all that hidden meaning?
I'm experienced. Dealt with Jinhsi's riddles already.
Thanks to my big brain.
Abby: But the buildings in Hongzhen all look pretty much the same. Which one exactly was she talking about?
We can ask around to find out. I've done this before.
Abby: Makes sense. Lead the way!
(Optional - Talk to Grandpa Zou again)
Grandpa Zou seems to be telling another story...
Grandpa Zou: ... With a wave of (‍‍hisText for male Rover‍/‍herText for female Rover‍‍) hand, Mianlong Chamber bursted open! The Sentinel awoke from its deep slumber, breaking through the clouds with unstoppable force!
Grandpa Zou: The Tacet Discords froze under its intimidating aura, unable to cause further harm.
Grandpa Zou: As the clouds dispersed and light returned to Mt. Firmament, the people were safe once more.
Perplexed Audience: This story you're telling today... It sounds a bit different from yesterday, doesn't it?
Curious Spectator: Hmm... so, which version is the real one?
Cheerful Spectator: Haha, who cares? Today's story sounds more entertaining than yesterday's. That's all I care about!
(Talk to Qihong)
Qihong: What can I help you with?
(Ask about the riddle in Changli's note.)
Qihong: "When snow thaw into streams"? Ah, you're not from around here, I bet? When we say that in Hongzhen, we mean the ShichenTime Period of Wei. Early afternoon, the warmest hours of a day.
Qihong: Legend tells of a visitor who ventured here some centuries ago. Back then, local villagers were struggling with no firewood due to heavy snow. This visitor opened up a path with their Forte and diverted a hot spring to provide warmth and aid.
Qihong: People say it was once a stunning sight, with mist and ice flowing westward down the streams, as if many celestial beings were returning to the sea. Now the sight has unfortunately disappeared, but the saying sticks. We use it to describe time in local speech.
I see.
Qihong: Well, it's what Grandpa Zou tells everyone. I haven't seen it with my own eyes, but when it comes to stories like this one... They're usually made-up.
You're such a great storyteller, like everyone else I met here.
Qihong: Oh please, I'm only repeating what I've heard from him. He's been on a roll with his stories lately. But let's not take them too seriously, they're just for entertainment.
You don't believe in those stories?
Qihong: Hmm... Not that I don't want to believe them, but... Oh, you were listening to one of his stories earlier too, right? What did you think?
It sounded interesting.
Qihong: Really? So you're into stories and anecdotes too?
It was a bit too exaggerated.
Qihong: Looks like we have that in common.
I wasn't mentioned in the story, so a thumbs down.
Qihong: Haha... Maybe Grandpa Zou can learn a thing or two from you in terms of humor.
Qihong: Grandpa Zou's great-grandfather was a descendant of the first inhabitants of Hongzhen. He grew up hearing stories about Mt. Firmament. Recently he heard Madam Magistrate had resolved the crisis, so he decided to visit and learn more about his roots.
Qihong: People in town are curious about the outside world and how they are perceived. Grandpa Zou is happy to answer their questions and has unknowingly become popular among them. Before he knew it, everyone was coming to talk to him...
And it turned into a storytelling session...
He must be a fan of that storyteller in Jinzhou.
Qihong: It's funny to hear outsiders describe my hometown, Hongzhen, as mysterious. We're just a normal place with our own quirks...
Qihong: Especially lately, with so many people from Jinzhou coming on some kind of expedition. They're obsessed with us, like we're some kind of ancient relics. Can you believe they actually asked if our Pavo Plums have magical powers?
Qihong: Time truly is a formidable force...
(Optional - Talk to Qihong again)
Qihong: What else can I do for you?
About Grandpa Zou...
Qihong: Grandpa Zou seems to have boundless energy, doesn't he? He arrived with an old, tattered book and told us he wanted to reconnect with his family. None of us knew him though.
Qihong: I gave him a tour of Hongzhen, and then we became quite close. As it turns out, we're actually related.
Qihong: However... I'm still unsure about how to address him as a family member... Regardless, it's a pleasant discovery to make.
Thank you, I'm good.
(Talk to the Suspicious Young Man)
Suspicious Young Man: What do you want? I've done nothing wrong!
(Ask about the riddle in Changli's note.)
Suspicious Young Man: Huh? Uh... You're just asking for directions...? Sorry, I'm not a local, can't help you there.
Suspicious Young Man: Wait, you... you were the one talking to Lady Changli earlier, weren't you?
The young man begins looking around warily, as if in fear of something terrible hidden in the shadows.
Suspicious Young Man: If I were you, I'd steer clear of her. She's a deceitful woman who enjoys toying with people's hearts. A cunning villain who will manipulate you without you even knowing it.
How so?
Suspicious Young Man: Haven't you heard? She left her government job to come here, to this small town. There's gotta be a reason behind it. Suspicious Young Man: I heard she chose to quit her job, but I bet she messed up back in the capital and got demoted here as punishment.
...It's not nice to badmouth people like this.
Not everyone values power and fame.
Suspicious Young Man: Then I guess you've also been fooled by her looks. That woman will stop at nothing to get what she wants, while you remain oblivious to her true intentions. And by the time you catch on, you'll already be caught in her trap.
Suspicious Young Man: Wait a minute, has she actually achieved anything substantial during her time in Jinzhou? Or did Madam Magistrate just fall for her clever words and let her slack off?
You're underestimating Jinhsi.
Suspicious Young Man: Hmph... I say you're underestimating Changli's trickery.
What makes you so sure?
Suspicious Young Man: I... I have my reasons to believe so!
Suspicious Young Man: I heard she tricked that VIP guest of Jinzhou into going to Mt. Firmament. Just think about how dangerous that place was!
Suspicious Young Man: She must have been afraid of her getting too close to Madam Magistrate and ruining her plans... What a sinister woman! Fortunately, that guest was a skilled fighter, and she managed to escape unharmed.
Suspicious Young Man: I hope you don't mind my frankness. Just giving some advice, 'cause you look pretty innocent and gullible... Not from Jinzhou judging by your outfit, right?
I am that VIP guest.
People call me Rover.
Suspicious Young Man: ...
Suspicious Young Man: ...
Suspicious Young Man: Oh shoot, I completely forgot about something I need to do. Sorry, gotta run...
(Talk to the Youning)
Youning: Uhh... How did she disappear like that? Wait, are you that legendary Rover who saved Jinzhou?!
Youning: Ahem... what can I do for you?
(Ask about the riddle in Changli's note.)
Youning: Well, you've come to the right person! I'm here to compile a new travel guide for Hongzhen!
Youning: "Next to a ring and hanging eaves" ... Oh! I know where that is. You'll need to stand on the tallest building in Hongzhen to see what you're looking for.
The tallest building?
Youning: It's on the northeast side of the town, can't miss it. You'll see it once you get there.
Youning: Say, that person earlier... that was Lady Changli, right?! I saw you talking to her!
Yes.
Do you know her?
Youning: I can't help but feel envious. I wish I could speak to her like you did, but she refuses to do interviews with the Pioneer Association. Plus, I doubt we have anything in common to talk about anyway.
Youning: Of course! Everyone in Jinzhou knows about Lady Changli, even though she rarely appears in public.
Youning: As Master Xuanmiao's disciple, she excels in the arts of politics and diplomacy. Her travels have taken her across the four seas, and as Secretary-General, she has commanded respect from all who cross her path!
Really?
Youning: Yeah! And she came all the way to Jinzhou to help out Magistrate Jinhsi for the sake of peace in Huanglong. She's been working tirelessly behind the scenes since then, fully dedicated to her task...
Youning: How could anyone not revere such a selfless act?
Youning: *sigh* I could've sworn I just saw her. Where did she go? I wish I could take one more look...
Are you sure you're just here for the travel guide?
Youning: Ahaha...
(Optional - Talk to Youning again)
Youning: Sigh... Looks like I've lost track of her again. Fine, I'll go back to work...
Youning: Hmm? Where did our photographer go this time?
Abby: Hey. Why are the people here so divided about Changli?
She doesn't seem to have ill intents.
We'll have to figure it out ourselves.
Abby: Hmm... You humans make everything so complicated.
Abby: Well, at least now we know what she wanted to say.
"Let's meet at the highest place in Hongzhen, in the early afternoon."
Abby: Now that's much easier to understand. Why did she have to make it a whole riddle? *yawn *... I'm getting sleepy again.
Xinyi: Rover?
Xinyi: Nice to see you again. How are you liking Hongzhen so far?
It's nice. The place is bustling with life.
It's much more lively than before.
Xinyi: The crisis at Mt. Firmament has been resolved, and the waterway between Jinzhou and Hongzhen is open once again. As a result, there has been an increase in visitors from Jinzhou, making the town more lively than before.
Xinyi: With the chaos subsiding, our town and city are now reconnected, allowing residents to live and work in peace.
Xinyi: We owe you a debt of gratitude, Rover, for your efforts in clearing the remaining effects of Temporal Disruptions in Mt. Firmament over the past few days.
Just doing my part.
Couldn't have done it without everyone.
That job was a beast. You better have my money ready.
Xinyi: *chuckle* Of course.
Xinyi: We're all indebted to you, Hongzhen and its people alike. If there's anything you need, don't hesitate to ask.
Xinyi: I couldn't help but notice you've been asking around. Is there something you need assistance with?
(Xinyi and Changli have a mutual trust as acquaintances. It should be fine to ask Xinyi instead...)
Well...
You tell Xinyi about your encounter with Changli and what the passersby said about her.
Xinyi: Hmm... I see. That sounds like something Changli would do.
Xinyi: Even though we're not that close, I know a bit about her personality. She wouldn't just hand over something that symbolizes her identity to anyone, especially when...
Especially what?
Xinyi: I think it would be better for her to tell you personally.
Xinyi: The Magistrate's Counselor is shrouded in mystery, and her motives are often hard to decipher...
Xinyi: When she wants something done, it's never as straightforward as it seems, and few can grasp the true meaning behind her plans.
Xinyi: The rumors and controversies surrounding her never cease, but she seems unfazed.
Xinyi: However... I believe one has to get involved personally to truly understand Changli's intentions, regardless of public opinion.
My plans exactly.
I'm very curious about her plans.
Xinyi: About the riddle... it seems you have already figured it out by yourself.
Xinyi: But remember, it's not just about the answer, but also what she wants you to understand.
Indeed.
Xinyi: *chuckle* Then ... If you'll excuse me.
Xinyi: If there's anything else you need here in Hongzhen, please do not hesitate to let me know.
Thank you.
(Head to the designated location)
Rover: (A ring, she wrote... Should be this ring-shaped ancient structure, I guess?)
Abby: Wow, it's really huge now that we look at it.
Rover: Next, hanging eaves... If we look from here... Is it that pavilion?
Abby: It does look quiet. Should be a nice place for meetings... *yawn* Ugh, getting 'eepy again...
Rover: That must be the place, then.
Rover: I'll get going.
(Head to the Pavillion at 13:00-15:00)
Changli: Apologies for my delay.
It's fine. I just got here too.
Something tells me you've been here for a while.
Changli: You looked adorable, focusing on the Weiqi board. I didn't want to interrupt you.
Changli: Thank you for accepting my invitation.
I see you really love your riddles.
Changli: Oh? And what makes you think so?
Rover: Those tokens from Jinhsi... It was your idea, was it not?
Changli: *chuckle *...So you've guessed it.
Changli: Sorry, (‍RoverThe player's chosen name for Rover‍). Jinzhou faced multiple threats back then, and we had to be cautious. We did not intend to inconvenience you. I regret our lack of hospitality.
It's okay. Jinhsi had explained your reasons.
I'm more or less used to it by now...
It's a thing of the past.
Changli: Still, I owe you an apology in person.
Changli: This time... *chuckle* I just wanted to see you. The brilliant mind that always understood my unspoken words.
Changli: ...I am very grateful you decided to come.
What's the deal this time? Another Tacet Discord to beat?
Changli: Apologies for giving you that impression, Rover. That's not how we treat our saviors.
What's the deal this time? Another errand to run?
Changli: Apologies for giving you that impression, Rover. That's not how we treat our saviors.
Let's cut to the chase. What do you want from me?
Changli: I merely have a few questions, and I was wondering if you may have the answers.
Changli: Does this game of WeiqiGo look familiar to you, Rover?
No.
Changli: ...I see.
...I'm not sure.
Changli: ... Apologies. I heard about your memory loss. Please pardon me.
Changli: There is a local tale about the "Secret of Immortality" being hidden on Mt. Firmament. Have you heard about it?
The one I heard in Hongzhen?
Changli: Yes. I have a slightly different version of this tale to share.
Changli: Centuries ago, a Taoist cultivator met an enigmatic visitor on Mt. Firmament. Despite their age difference, they soon became friends and often played Weiqi together.
Changli: One day, a woodcutter stumbled upon them, having lost his way home. Their game mesmerized him so much that he didn't notice the red tie on his basket rotting away... Panicked, he bumped into the Weiqi board.
Changli: Despite the interruption, the visitor remained unfazed. They offered the woodcutter some tea, then guided him down the mountain, shielding him from dangerous Temporal Disruptions. After that, the visitor disappeared.
Changli: Many years later, the Taoist cultivator became a legendary hermit guru. Upon returning to Mt. Firmament in his final years, he reunited with that elusive visitor.
Changli: The two resumed their unfinished game. People believe the visitor shared their Secret of Immortality through cleverly-placed Weiqi pieces, as a final parting gift.
You mean this game in front of us?
Changli: Yes... and no. This game is missing the final twenty moves. It is unfinished.
Changli: That was a bit different from what you heard before, I guess? The story changed over time, infused with fantasy in each retelling.
Changli: But that's how old tales go, slowly losing their truth as they're passed down.
You mean the other folklores may hold some truth too.
Changli: Precisely.
Changli: The legend may be shrouded in myth, but that game of Weiqi was real. Embedded within its records lies a cryptic message: "This game record can solve the crisis of time."
Changli: From what I know, only the Sentinel in its prime has the power to manipulate time through its possession of a complete Temporal Mandate. For us mere mortals, controlling time is indeed similar to gaining immortality.
Changli: As the records state, it only reveals itself when Mt. Firmament emerges. But how it ties to the Temporal Mandate remains an enigma... at least for now.
The Sentinel's wounds...
Changli: Yes. We may find a way to heal them.
There might be an undamaged sample of Temporal Mandate.
Changli: If that is the case, we'll be able to heal the Sentinel's wounds.
Changli: But... our chances are looking slim. That game record could just hold my teacher's memories, not any real value.
Changli: So I am presenting this as merely a personal request.
Changli: I am planning to go find that record. Could you please join me?
Sure.
Changli: Thank you for lending me a hand. I promise it will be worth your while.
I am interested in this tale too.
Why me?
Changli: As we have been to Mt. Firmament before, I imagined it would pique your interest, as the tale concerns our Sentinel.
Changli: And, moreover... You are special to me, and... to Mt. Firmament. I hope I have provided enough reasons to clear your doubts.
Special?
Changli: I asked you about the unfinished Weiqi game, because I believe it may have something to do with your past.
You mean...
Changli: Yes... After all, it takes two to play Weiqi, right?
I see. Then I suppose I have no reason to not go.
I'll consider it, but what's in it for me?
Changli: If my speculation is correct... That game of Weiqi may hold clues to your lost memories.
Changli: In addition... I promise to aid you in any way I can after we return with the record. How does that sound?
I see. Then I have no reason to not go.
Alright. Count me in!
Changli: Splendid.
It's still early. How about we set off now?
Changli: Very well. Let's meet on the gallery road outside Hongzhen.
Changli: I still have some preparations to do. Please go ahead, I'll join you later.
(Head to the designated location)
Changli: Rover, you're here.
Wasn't expecting you to arrive before me.
Changli: Well... As the Wayfinder, I do know a couple shortcuts.
I trust you'll guide me well, Miss Wayfinder.
Where are we going?
Changli: The notes only provided a vague idea of where the game record is. I've determined the most likely location on my last visit.
Changli: We'll be heading there. See if we can find anything new.
You've been there before?
That's surprisingly straightforward, especially coming from you.
Changli: After dealing with those Artificers, I ruled out the other locations on my way to join you.
Changli: But one can only do so much alone. This is why I need your help.
Lucky for you, I'm very good at finding things.
Gotta throw myself a challenge from time to time.
I'm not planning to go back on my own words.
Changli: How reliable.
Changli: Then let's get going.
(Head to the designated location)
Changli: ...
Rover: Changli? What is it?
Changli: Nothing, (‍RoverThe player's chosen name for Rover‍). I just thought... the snow is beautiful today.
(Head to the designated location)
Changli: You seem curious about that ancient structure.
Rover: It looks familiar... Like the abandoned Court of Savantae facility I saw, but bigger in scale.
Changli: I heard it first appeared along with our Sentinel. Later, the Court of Savantae based their Chronosorters on its design.
(Head to the designated location)
Changli: Every winter, my hometown buzzed as people left their mark in the fresh snow, hoping for dreams to come true when it melted.
Rover: Did you try it too, Changli?
Changli: No, I only watched from afar... My Forte always melted the snow faster than I liked.
(Head to the designated location)
Changli: We can see the whole of Hongzhen from here.
Changli: I never noticed how beautiful it looked during my previous visits.
Changli: It's the same place as always. I suppose it's my state of mind that has changed.
How did it change?
Changli: I don't know. Maybe it's because... Your presence makes me feel at ease.
Abby: Wait... I smell Tacet Discords in that cave!
Abby: No... There's more... Tacet Discords, humans, and...
Abby: Smells like a whole bunch of messed up frequencies... It's so... familiar...
(How could there be any Tacet Discords in Mt. Firmament?)
(ls Abby sleep talking again?)
Abby: C'mon, after all we've been through, you still don't trust my sniffer? Be grateful, I'm giving you a warning!
Changli: Rover? Did something happen?
Tacet Discords could be assaulting people over there.
Changli: It's in the same direction we're going. Could it be...
Let's go take a look.
(Head to the designated location)
Changli: Signs of climbing... Someone may have been here before us.
(Enter the cave)
Explorer: Get away... from me! Ugh... I can't hold up much longer...
(Defeat the TDs)
Explorer: Help, help! Oh, thank goodness...
Changli: Please stand back. We'll take it from here.
Explorer: I-I can fight! Let me help!
(Optional - Investigate the glowing spot on the ground)
A compass burried in the ground. It resembles those commonly used by the Pioneer Association.
(Talk to the Explorer)
Explorer: T-Thanks for your help...
Are you all right?
Explorer: I... I'm okay. Wait, you... Are you THE Rover...?
How do you know me?
Explorer: You're that hero who fought against the Threnodian, and you also resolved the time crisis here with Madam Magistrate. Everyone's been talking about you...
Explorer: And Lady Changli ... I-I never thought I'd have the chance to see you in person...
Explorer: ...Without your help, I would've been a goner for sure...
Explorer: I can't die here. Not when I've got someone waiting for me...
Explorer: I've finally, finally found it... After all this time... Ugh...
Take it easy. Everything's all right.
Relax. Your wounds look pretty bad.
Changli: While we've solved the crisis in Mt. Firmament for the time being... Public access to the mountain is still restricted. Before entering the mountain, any explorer must submit a request and can only do so while accompanied by the Midnight Rangers.
Changli: Sir, could you please share your reasons for traveling here alone?
Explorer: I, I heard about Mt. Firmament's legend... So I came to find its secret...
Explorer: I've only been in the mountain for half a day, everything was going smoothly before those monsters pounced on me on my way back... *cough *...
Explorer: I must get back... Fuling... She's still waiting for me...
He doesn't look like he's only been here for half a day...
Changli: It seems he is still hiding something from us.
He seems a bit off.
Changli: Some of those injuries are older than half a day...
Changli: He needs to go back to Hongzhen for proper medical attention... Time is against us.
We'll need to escort him down the mountain.
Changli: Agreed.
